body.name: terminal_input

definition.name: terminal_input
definition.description: Accepts and stores the input from terminal. This is a legacy primitive because the meaning stops at this layer (even though it is built from more primitives) but I am establishing it as a primitive because I haven't yet constructed this meaning from computable semantic primitives.
definition._note: This primitive throws an EOFError and Keyboard Interrupt error. EOFError can be triggered by using CTRL+D in unix environments and Ctrl+Z followed by Enter in windows. Keyboard interrupts happen when Ctrl + C is used to terminate program in console. The meaning of these errors are built into the primitive and as part of the narrative that uses them the relevant behavior that should be exhibited can be specified. So in the synthesized implementation, I will throw the errors and then the specified meaning is used.
definition._note2: I will extend the syntax for the errors after I implement the necessary functionality.

definition.name: list_contains
definition.description: For participants with structural type list, it establishes the role of the participants that the list can contain.
definition._note: When a participant has a particular structural type, there are other meta attributes like list_contains which need to be included to complete the meaning of the list structural type. The engine needs to be able to identify if this is missing, so I need to establish the types for the participants and the attributes that must be specified.

definition.name: equals
definition.description: Checks if two values are equal.
definition._note: There are some corner cases where this primitive can be incorrect. For example, when adding two floats and checking equality (ex 0.1 + 0.2 == 0.3) causes floating point issues. Poorly implemented _eq_ methods can also cause issues. However, in this case, since I am synthesizing the implementation, I use the participants directly in the equality and this since I also synthesize the participants, I can account for the _eq_ methods. I am leaving this note here so I am aware of these issues with the realization of this meaning.
